results.root_cause_actual: PR #881 (commit 3f0ab155) simultaneously raised the api-gateway PaymentsClient read timeout from 3s to 30s AND disabled the circuit breaker for payments-svc. When the partner acquirer degraded to p99=12.4s at 18:47Z, both fast-failure mechanisms were absent. Each payment worker thread was held for up to 30s (10× longer than before), while the ALB proxy_read_timeout remained at 10s — meaning the client received a 504 at 10s but the gateway thread stayed blocked for the remaining ~20s. The mismatch between the 30s gateway read timeout and the 10s ALB proxy_read_timeout meant threads were never released promptly even after the client was gone. All 64 worker threads saturated with blocked PaymentsClient.execute() calls by 18:51Z, exhausting the shared thread pool (which is also used by all other routes), causing gateway-wide 504s including routes that do not call payments-svc (/v1/orders, /v1/catalog).
results.root_cause_expected: PR #881 raised the gateway's payments-svc read timeout from 3s to 30s (and disabled the circuit breaker) while the edge load balancer's proxy_read_timeout stayed at 10s. When partner latency rose, the edge cut clients off at 10s with 504s while gateway worker threads stayed pinned on the upstream call for the full 30s, saturating the 64-thread pool and taking down routes that never touch payments-svc.

judge.reason: Both identify the same underlying cause: PR #881 raised the gateway payments-svc read timeout to 30s while disabling the circuit breaker, creating a mismatch with the 10s ALB proxy_read_timeout that caused threads to remain pinned after clients disconnected, saturating the shared thread pool and affecting all routes.

mechanism: PR #881 deployed api-gateway v9.2.0 at 18:40:00Z, raising PAYMENTS_READ_TIMEOUT from 3s to 30s and disabling the payments circuit breaker.
At 18:47Z, partner acquirer p99 latency climbed to 12.4s — a degradation that, under v9.1.7, would have caused fast 3s timeouts and circuit-breaker trips.
With the new 30s timeout and no circuit breaker, each payment request now held its worker thread open for up to 30s waiting on the slow acquirer.
The ALB proxy_read_timeout remained at 10s; ALB therefore returned 504 to the client after 10s, but the gateway thread remained blocked on the upstream call for the remaining ~20s.
Threads accumulated faster than they were released: at 18:50Z 58/64 were busy, at 18:51Z all 64 were blocked in PaymentsClient.execute(), and the accept queue grew to 611.

With all worker threads saturated by payments calls, the gateway could not process any new requests — including routes with no payments-svc dependency (/v1/orders, /v1/catalog) — causing gateway-wide 504s and availability dropping to 88.1%.

ruled_out.candidate: Partner acquirer degradation as sole root cause
ruled_out.why_not: The acquirer degradation is a trigger, not the root cause. The deployment notes explicitly state 'Under v9.1.7 these calls failed fast at 3s' — the same acquirer slowdown would not have caused thread saturation under the previous config because threads would have been released within 3s and the circuit breaker would have opened. The acquirer degradation only became catastrophic because of the config changes in PR #881.

ruled_out.candidate: ALB proxy_read_timeout mismatch (10s < 30s) as root cause
ruled_out.why_not: The ALB 10s timeout causing 504s to clients is a contributing symptom amplifier, not the root cause. The critical failure mode is thread pool exhaustion from 30s-held threads, not the ALB timeout itself. The ALB timeout has been 10s since 2024 and was unchanged; it alone cannot exhaust gateway threads.

ruled_out.candidate: Insufficient gateway worker thread count (64 threads)
ruled_out.why_not: Thread count was unchanged at 64 before and after the deploy (GATEWAY_WORKER_THREADS 64 -> 64 unchanged). Pre-deploy only 9 threads were busy. The saturation is caused by each thread being held 30s rather than 3s — a 10x increase in thread hold time — not by insufficient thread capacity.

red_herrings.candidate: ALB proxy_read_timeout mismatch (10s) as the root cause in isolation
red_herrings.why_not: The ALB 10s timeout has been in place since 2024 and was unchanged (deployment.txt: 'This value has been 10s since 2024 and was not touched by PR #881'). It is a contributing factor that worsens thread hold time, but the primary cause is the 30s gateway read timeout + disabled circuit breaker holding threads long after clients have disconnected.

red_herrings.candidate: Partner acquirer degradation as sole root cause
red_herrings.why_not: deployment.txt explicitly states 'Under v9.1.7 these calls failed fast at 3s' — the same acquirer degradation would not have saturated the thread pool under previous configuration. The acquirer is a trigger that exposed the config change, not the root cause.

cross_file_value_checks.governs: payment request lifecycle: ALB waits 10s for gateway to respond, but gateway thread holds upstream connection for up to 30s
cross_file_value_checks.note: ALB abandons the client-facing request after 10s and returns 504, but the gateway worker thread stays blocked on PaymentsClient.execute() for up to 30s. This means each slow payment request consumes a thread for ~30s even though the client gets a 504 at 10s — the thread is held 3x longer than the client-visible timeout, causing thread-pool exhaustion.

cross_file_value_checks.governs: thread pool capacity vs. thread hold time per slow payment request
cross_file_value_checks.note: At p99=29.9s per call and 64 total threads, even a modest payment request rate saturates the pool. Pre-deploy with 3s timeout the same 64 threads cycled ~10x faster per thread-slot, keeping headroom available.

cross_file_value_checks.governs: whether slow acquirer calls fail fast or hold threads
cross_file_value_checks.note: 30s timeout exceeds acquirer p99 of 12.4s, so threads are not released until the full slow response (or timeout) completes rather than failing fast at 3s as previously.
With circuit breaker disabled, there is no mechanism to stop issuing slow upstream calls during acquirer degradation; under v9.1.7 the breaker would have opened and shed load immediately.

cross_file_value_checks.governs: fast-failure safety net for payment calls
cross_file_value_checks.note: Both changes were made together, simultaneously removing the primary (circuit breaker) and secondary (short timeout) fast-failure mechanisms for payments-svc calls.
All 64 threads saturated; accept queue grew to 611, confirming all new requests (including non-payment routes) were queued and ultimately rejected or timed out.

meta.unresolved: The exact line '+    circuitBreaker: disabled' does not appear verbatim in the diff (the diff shows '-    circuitBreaker: enabled' and '+    circuitBreaker: disabled' but with leading spaces; the proposed root cause cited it without the leading spaces). Otherwise the causal chain is fully supported. One minor ambiguity: the mechanism by which threads remain blocked after the ALB returns 504 (i.e., Java HttpClient not being notified of client disconnect) is implied by the 'Broken pipe' error and the 29.9s upstream hold log line but is not explicitly stated in the artifacts as a JVM/library behavior.
